stem: Small, white to yellow raised sebaceous glands appear as spots in hairless areas of the body. What is the name for these spots?
rationale: Fordyce granules have a raised, yellow to white hue and are ectopic sebaceous glands. Lichen planus exhibits a white lacy appearance, morsicatio buccarum exhibits an irritated/macerated appearance, and leukoedema has a blue opalescent appearance that disappears when stretched.

stem: Lichen planus that exhibits a white lacy appearance is termed:
rationale: Reticular lichen planus is the most common form and characteristically exhibits Wickham striae (a white lacy appearance). Atrophic and erosive forms present with red, irritated, or ulcerative surfaces.

stem: The varicella-zoster virus causes which of the following?
rationale: Shingles (herpes zoster) is caused by reactivation of the latent varicella-zoster virus. Herpes labialis and primary herpetic gingivostomatitis are caused by HSV-1; herpangina is caused by coxsackievirus.

stem: One characteristic associated with a differentiation of Fordyce granules and cheek bites is which of the following:

options.a: Both are found in all age groups
options.b: When the tissue is stretched, opalescence disappears
options.c: It is found in the buccal mucosa
options.d: Both may have a white/yellow hue in appearance

rationale: Intracellular edema is responsible for leukoedema and will disappear when the tissue is stretched. Morsicatio buccarum (cheek biting) exhibits macerated tissue that will not disappear upon stretching.

stem: Fordyce granules are ectopic sebaceous granules and affect most adults but are not found in those who have not reached puberty. This is due to:
rationale: Fordyce granules respond to androgenic hormones during puberty, which is why both adolescent males and females begin developing them at puberty, but they are absent in young children.

stem: The irritation fibroma is most often found in certain oral areas. Which choice best describes the location?

options.c: Areas of high trauma such as the lips, tongue, and gingiva

rationale: Areas of high trauma such as the labial mucosa, tongue, buccal mucosa along the occlusal line, and gingiva experience chronic bite trauma leading to irritation fibromas.

stem: The most common age group for an irritation fibroma is:

options.a: Adolescent ages in both males and females

rationale: Irritation fibromas are most commonly diagnosed in adult females in their 40s to 60s (such as a 45-year-old female) along the bite line over time.

stem: A mucocele is not a true cyst because of which of the following?

options.a: The mucin is surrounded with granulation tissue.
options.b: The mucin is surrounded with connective tissue.
options.c: The mucin is not surrounded with epithelium.
options.d: The salivary duct is dilated due to epithelial thickening.

rationale: A true cyst must be lined by epithelium. Mucoceles are pseudocysts formed by spilled mucin into connective tissue lined only by granulation tissue.

stem: When the mucocele or Extravasation Phenomenon occurs in the floor of the mouth affecting the sublingual or submandibular glands, the correct term would be which of the following?
rationale: A ranula is the clinical term for a large mucocele located in the floor of the mouth affecting the sublingual or submandibular gland ducts.

stem: A white line that extends from the anterior to the buccal mucosa caused by the impact of occlusion is called:
rationale: Linea alba is a linear white keratinized line along the buccal mucosa positioned directly along the occlusal plane.

stem: Nicotine stomatitis denotes irritation of the minor salivary glands. Where does this occur?
rationale: Nicotine stomatitis affects the hard palate where minor salivary gland openings become inflamed and reddened due to heat and smoke.

stem: Which of the following would not be the etiology in the development of the torus palatinus?
rationale: Bacterial and viral infections are not etiologic factors. Torus palatinus is caused by genetic predisposition, masticatory forces, and bone trauma/stresses.

stem: The torus mandibularis most often is observed in which age group?

options.a: Females in the 20- to 30-year-old age group
options.b: Males in the 13- to 16-year-old age group
options.d: Males in the 20- to 30-year age group

rationale: Torus mandibularis is typically diagnosed in young adults and teens (such as males in the 13- to 16-year-old age group).

stem: A patient who has the mandibular right and left premolars congenitally missing is probably suffering with which of the disorders listed below?
rationale: Ectodermal dysplasia is an inherited syndrome characterized by hypodontia (congenitally missing teeth such as premolars), along with hair, skin, and sweat gland abnormalities.

stem: All of the following are a contributing factor in Lingua villosa (Hairy Tongue) EXCEPT one. Which one is the EXCEPTION?

options.a: Radiation to the head and neck
options.d: Consumption of excessive xylitol products such as gum and mints

rationale: Consumption of xylitol products does not cause hairy tongue. Radiation therapy, PPIs, alcohol, smoking, and antibiotics are known contributing factors.

stem: Two roots fused together in the cementum is called:
rationale: Concrescence is a form of developmental fusion where two adjacent teeth are united only by root cementum.

stem: The Pleomorphic adenoma accounts for what percentage of all salivary gland tumors?
rationale: Pleomorphic adenoma accounts for up to 90% of all benign salivary gland tumors, occurring most commonly in the parotid gland.

stem: The Thyroglossal Tract Cyst is located in the midline of the neck. Which of the tasks performed by a dental hygienist is the most important in identifying this cyst? Select the best answer.
rationale: A thorough thyroid and neck examination involving clinical palpation is the best method for detecting a midline thyroglossal tract cyst early.

stem: The age range of a person who develops a thyroglossal tract cyst is:
rationale: Thyroglossal tract cysts develop along the path of embryonic thyroid descent and are usually diagnosed in young adults under 20 years of age.

stem: Which of the following is NOT true for the pleomorphic adenoma?

options.a: It occurs most commonly in adults
options.b: It occurs in the submandibular gland
options.c: There is a 5% malignant transformation rate

rationale: Pleomorphic adenoma occurs in the parotid gland most often, not the submandibular gland.

stem: The most commonly occurring odontogenic cyst is:
rationale: Periapical (radicular) cysts are the most common odontogenic cysts. Dentigerous cysts are the second most common.

stem: The cause of a residual cyst is:
rationale: A residual cyst forms when a radicular/periapical cyst is left behind following improper or incomplete tooth extraction.

stem: The simple bone cyst is treated using which of the following protocols?

options.d: Endodontic treatment for the nonvital tooth

rationale: Surgical curettage causes bleeding and clot formation, stimulating bone regeneration to fill the cavity within about six months.

stem: Sickle Cell Anemia is predominately found in African American Populations. However, this may be found in other populations as well. Which group listed below is also susceptible to this disorder?
rationale: Both African American and Mediterranean/Asian populations are susceptible to sickle cell gene mutations.

stem: Which of the following is a major risk factor for oropharyngeal cancer in the tonsillar region?
rationale: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is a major oncogenic virus known to promote oropharyngeal cancer in the tonsillar and base-of-tongue regions.

stem: Pernicious Anemia is also known as:
rationale: Plummer-Vinson syndrome is associated with mucosal atrophy and iron deficiency, while pernicious anemia stems from intrinsic factor deficiency.

stem: A patient who is experiencing a loss of filiform papillae, angular cheilitis, pallor of the oral mucosa and burning of the tongue may be deficient in which of the following?
rationale: Iron deficiency anemia presents with mucosal pallor, angular cheilitis, loss of filiform papillae (glossitis), and burning sensation.

stem: The most common oral implication of HIV is:
rationale: Oral candidiasis occurs early in up to 85-90% of HIV cases. Kaposi sarcoma occurs in late-stage HIV (15-20%).

stem: The abnormal Philadelphia 22 chromosome is associated with which of the following?
rationale: The Philadelphia chromosome (abnormality of chromosome 22) is the diagnostic marker for Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (CML).

stem: Cherubism is an inherited autosomal dominant disorder predominately in females. It is a defect of SH3BP2 gene. The disorder is usually found in which age group of patients?
rationale: Cherubism is diagnosed in very young children, sometimes as young as one to five years old.

stem: The patient with Cherubism is at risk for which of the following?
rationale: Patients with cherubism are monitored for potential malignant sarcomatous transformations or aggressive giant cell lesions.

stem: The patient who is at risk for pemphigoid should be evaluated for which of the following?
rationale: Mucous membrane pemphigoid involves ocular tissues and can cause severe conjunctival scarring and eye damage.

stem: Osteomalacia means “soft bones,” but what is the term used for adults who have demineralization of bones?
rationale: Osteopenia refers to demineralization and reduced bone density developing over time in adults.

stem: The most likely area to witness Abfraction would be:

options.a: The incisal edge of the lower anterior teeth
options.c: The cervical areas of teeth at the CEJ

rationale: Abfraction produces wedge-shaped defects in the cervical areas of teeth at the Cementoenamel Junction (CEJ) due to flexural forces.

stem: Amelogenesis imperfecta is categorized into four types. Which type listed is the least common type?
rationale: Hypocalcified type represents a defect in mineralization of enamel matrix.

stem: The term for two roots fused together in the cementum is:
rationale: Concrescence is the union of two fully formed roots joined during root cementum formation.

stem: Dens invaginatus (Dens in Dente) occurs most frequently in which location?
rationale: Maxillary lateral incisors are the most common site for dens invaginatus.

stem: Geographic tongue (benign migratory glossitis) is associated with all of the following EXCEPT one. Which one is the EXCEPTION?
rationale: Geographic tongue is a benign condition with no malignancy component.

stem: Which is the common site of Fordyce granules?
rationale: The buccal mucosa is the most common intraoral site for Fordyce granules.

stem: Hairy tongue is associated with the elongation of which papillae?
rationale: Filiform papillae are the most numerous papillae on the tongue and become elongated in hairy tongue.

stem: Of the following diseases, in which one would you expect to see melanin production and the oral pigmentation associated with the disorder?
rationale: Addison disease (Primary Adrenal Insufficiency) stimulates melanin production, presenting with diffuse oral macular pigmentation.

stem: Teeth that are present at birth present as unstable, with undeveloped roots are termed:
rationale: Natal teeth are present at birth, developing from dental lamina with undeveloped roots, making them unstable.

stem: Clinical signs of Paget disease involve all of the following except which one?

options.c: More prevalent in African American males
options.d: There is a decrease in radiodensity

rationale: Paget disease occurs more often in Caucasian males, not African American males.

stem: Select the entity that exhibits signs of kidney stones, join pain, resorption of bone, Brown tumors, malocclusion, and loss of lamina dura.
rationale: Hyperparathyroidism / Osteomalacia manifests with inadequate mineralization of bone tissue, kidney stones, and Brown tumors.

stem: Hemophilia is a genetic autosomal dominant deficiency of clotting factors of Vlll or lX in the blood. What is the name associated with this disorder occurring in males and females?
rationale: Von Willebrand disease is an inherited clotting factor deficiency occurring in both males and females.

stem: The dentigerous cyst (follicular cyst) occurs around the crowns of an unerupted or developing tooth. They arise from a cystic change in the dental follicle. What other fact listed below is NOT commonly related to the dentigerous cyst?

options.a: The cyst is unilocular and sometimes multilocular
options.b: The most frequent location is the third molar region
options.c: The dentigerous cyst commonly occurs in the 20 to 30 age range
options.d: It is the most common type of an inflammatory odontogenic cyst

rationale: The dentigerous cyst is classified as a developmental cyst, not an inflammatory odontogenic cyst.

stem: The Nasolabial cyst that is found in the soft tissues of the lip lateral to the midline, in the mucolabial fold near the maxillary canine, and in the floor of the nose is categorized as:
rationale: The nasolabial cyst is a developmental soft tissue cyst.

stem: Most people will clear the HPV virus in time. What is the usual amount of time for clearance to occur?
rationale: Twelve months (1 to 2 years) is the typical amount of time for spontaneous HPV clearance in immunocompetent individuals.

stem: A simple bone cyst will usually be seen on radiograph as a large area of the mandible. The descriptor that is most appropriate is which of the following?

options.c: A scalloped appearance encircling the roots of existing teeth

rationale: Simple bone cysts present radiographically with a characteristic scalloped radiolucent margin encircling tooth roots.

stem: What is the most common type of oral lichen planus?
rationale: Reticular type is the most common clinical form of oral lichen planus (erosive form presents with intense intraoral lesions on attached gingiva).
